Parameters_and_Variables: W_q = Mean waiting time in queue; rho = Server utilization (traffic intensity); C_a = Coefficient of variation of inter-arrival times; C_s = Coefficient of variation of service times; mu = Mean service rate.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Kingman, J. F. C. (1961). The single server queue in heavy traffic. Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society, 57(4), 902–904; Kingman, J. F. C. (1962). On queues in heavy traffic. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 24(2), 383–392.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Establishes the fundamental theoretical queuing foundation of the thesis (H2): checkpoint queues scale quadratically with arrival volatility (C_a^2) as checkpoint utilization approaches capacity (rho -> 1.0), proving why predicting throughput volatility is operationally superior to predicting raw mean volume.

Parameters_and_Variables: W_q = Expected queue wait time; s = Number of active parallel screening lanes; rho = Multi-server utilization (lambda / (s*mu)); C_a = Arrival CV; C_s = Service time CV; mu = Lane processing rate.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Whitt, W. (1993). Approximations for the GI/G/m queue. Production and Operations Management, 2(2), 114–161; Marchal, W. G. (1976). An approximate formula for waiting time in GI/G/1. Operations Research, 24(3), 473–474.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Extends Kingman queuing principles to multi-lane airport security screening checkpoints (s parallel lanes), demonstrating buffer depletion under high lane utilization across Top 25 commercial airfields.

Parameters_and_Variables: rho(t) = Instantaneous traffic intensity at hour t; lambda(t) = Hourly passenger arrival demand rate; c(t) = Number of open screening lanes at hour t; mu = Nominal screening throughput rate per lane (pax/lane-hr).
Published_Source_and_Citation: Kendall, D. G. (1953). Stochastic processes occurring in the theory of queues and their analysis by the method of the imbedded Markov chain. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 24(3), 338–354; Erlang, A. K. (1909).
Thesis_Operational_Role: Operationalized in Chapter III Macro Filtering (§3.4): small regional airfields operate at rho << 0.30 (preventing queue formation), whereas Top 25 hubs routinely hit rho -> 1.0 during bank surges (05:00–08:30 and 16:00–18:30).

Mathematical_Formulation_Plain_Text: tau ~ Lognormal(mu, sigma^2), with E[tau] ≈ 105 minutes
Parameters_and_Variables: tau = Lead time (minutes before scheduled departure) that ticketed passengers present at security; mu = Log-scale mean; sigma = Log-scale dispersion; E[tau] = Expected show-up lead time (~105 minutes for domestic legacy flights).
Published_Source_and_Citation: Airport Cooperative Research Program (ACRP). (2010). ACRP Report 40: Airport Curbside and Terminal Area Planning. Transportation Research Board, National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Governs the empirical lead-lag passenger arrival distribution convolving scheduled flight banks into landside security arrival curves across American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines.

Equation_Name: Gaussian Mixture Bimodal Boarding Arrival Distribution
Mathematical_Formulation_Plain_Text: tau_WN ~ w1 * N(mu1, sigma1^2) + (1 - w1) * N(mu2, sigma2^2)
Parameters_and_Variables: tau_WN = Southwest passenger arrival lead time; w1 = Weight of boarding position maximizers (~135 min lead time); (1-w1) = Weight of carry-on business travelers (~65 min lead time).
Published_Source_and_Citation: ACRP Report 40 (TRB, 2010); Pearson, K. (1894). Contributions to the mathematical theory of evolution. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, 185, 71–110.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Empirically demonstrates that unassigned boarding produces bimodal arrival distributions, justifying Southwest Airlines exclusion under Meso Filtering to prevent passenger show-up heterogeneity.

Equation_Name: Local Originating Passenger Demand Accounting Identity
Mathematical_Formulation_Plain_Text: Demand_orig(t) = sum_{f in F_t} [ Seats_f * LoadFactor_f * (1 - ConnectingRatio_airport) ]
Parameters_and_Variables: Demand_orig,t = True originating passenger demand entering landside screening at hour t; Seats_f = Aircraft seat capacity for flight f; LoadFactor_f = Route-level passenger load factor; ConnectingRatio = Quarterly airport connecting percentage from DB1B.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS). (2024). Form 41 Schedule T-100 Segment Data and DB1B Airline Origin and Destination Survey. U.S. Department of Transportation.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Resolves the Hub Disconnect: subtracts transferring passengers who never enter landside security queues, increasing explained schedule-to-checkpoint variance from 20.9% to 44.9% across the Top 25 airfields.

Equation_Name: Discrete Empirical Lead-Time Convolution (Finite Impulse Response)
Parameters_and_Variables: w_h = Empirical ACRP arrival weights: w_1 (t+1 hr lead) = 0.52, w_2 (t+2 hr lead) = 0.38, w_3 (t+3 hr lead) = 0.10, where sum(w_h) = 1.0; F_{t+h} = Set of scheduled departures at hours t+1, t+2, t+3.
Published_Source_and_Citation: ACRP Report 40 (TRB, 2010); Oppenheim, A. V., & Schafer, R. W. (2009). Discrete-Time Signal Processing (3rd ed.). Prentice Hall.
Thesis_Operational_Role: The physical operational engine of Model 1 (Deterministic Flight Schedule Model), convolving scheduled departure banks into landside arrival hours to forecast baseline passenger demand.

Parameters_and_Variables: sigma_TSA,hr(d) = Diurnal standard deviation of hourly passenger screening throughput on day d (pax/hr); y_{d,h} = Hourly TSA throughput at hour h; y_bar_d = Daily mean hourly throughput.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Pearson, K. (1894). Contributions to the mathematical theory of evolution. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, 185, 71–110.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Primary dependent modeling target 1: captures within-day absolute demand dispersion across the 24 hours of each day (in pax/hr), isolating bank surge amplitudes.

Equation_Name: Intraday Scale-Free Relative Arrival Volatility (Coefficient of Variation)
Parameters_and_Variables: CV_TSA,hr = Dimensionless ratio of hourly standard deviation to daily mean throughput.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Pearson, K. (1895). Notes on regression and inheritance in the case of two parents. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, 58, 240–242.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Primary dependent modeling target 2: removes facility baseline scale to quantify pure arrival burstiness and queue surge spikiness across different checkpoint geometries.

Parameters_and_Variables: sigma_TSA,7d(d) = Rolling 7-day standard deviation of daily passenger volume (pax/day); Y_{d-k} = Total daily throughput on day d-k; Y_bar_7d = 7-day rolling mean daily throughput.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Box, G. E., Jenkins, G. M., Reinsel, G. C., & Ljung, G. M. (2015). Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control (5th ed.). John Wiley & Sons.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Primary dependent modeling target 3: captures medium-term multi-day network turbulence caused by severe winter storm systems, convective ground delay programs, and cancellation cascades.

Parameters_and_Variables: sigma_Delay,d = Sample standard deviation of flight departure delays across all uncancelled domestic departures on day d (minutes); DepDelay_i = Actual minus scheduled departure time for flight i; N_d = Total domestic departures.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Standard sample variance; Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS). (2024). Airline On-Time Performance Data Technical Reporting Directives.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Primary airside explanatory volatility metric: exhibits strong operational coupling with landside checkpoint arrival volatility (r = +0.4373, p < 0.05), while raw delay minutes show zero correlation (r = -0.062).

Parameters_and_Variables: RMSE = Quadratic loss forecast error (pax/hr); y_t = Actual observed volatility; y_hat_t = Model-predicted volatility; N = Sample evaluation hours.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Standard quadratic loss metric in statistical estimation and econometric forecasting.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Governing absolute error metric for Dimension 1 (Robustness): Model 3 achieves lowest RMSE (222.1 pax/hr) on the 2025 holdout dataset (-91.3 pax/hr vs Model 1).

Parameters_and_Variables: MAE = Linear loss forecast error (pax/hr); absolute difference between observed and predicted values.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Standard linear loss metric in time-series forecasting and regression.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Measures typical magnitude of point forecast errors without quadratic penalty for outliers; Model 3 achieves 142.8 pax/hr across dedicated screening complexes.

Parameters_and_Variables: Bias = Mean directional error (pax/hr); negative values indicate systematic under-prediction; positive values indicate over-prediction.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Standard forecast bias metric in operations research and inventory management.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Evaluates systematic under-prediction during bank surges: Model 1 displays -42.1 pax/hr bias; Model 2 exhibits -18.4 pax/hr; Model 3 maintains near-zero bias (-8.5 pax/hr).

Parameters_and_Variables: MASE = Scale-free relative forecast accuracy metric; numerator is candidate model MAE; denominator is in-sample mean absolute error of 24-hour diurnal naive persistence control.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Hyndman, R. J., & Koehler, A. B. (2006). Another look at measures of forecast accuracy. International Journal of Forecasting, 22(4), 679–688.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Primary scale-free benchmark metric across all models and regimes: Baseline Control is calibrated at MASE = 1.000; Model 2 achieves MASE = 0.779; Model 3 achieves champion MASE = 0.662.

Equation_Name: Diebold-Mariano Test Statistic for Equal Predictive Accuracy
Parameters_and_Variables: d_t = e_{1,t}^2 - e_{2,t}^2 (Loss differential at time t); d_bar = Sample mean loss differential; Var_hat(d_bar) = Asymptotic long-run variance of loss differential.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Diebold, F. X., & Mariano, R. S. (1995). Comparing predictive accuracy. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 13(3), 253–263.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Formally proves that Model 2 (DM = 42.15, p < 0.0001) and Model 3 (DM = 48.72, p < 0.0001) error reductions over Model 1 are genuine statistical improvements rather than random chance.

Equation_Name: Chow Test Statistic for Structural Breaks in Linear Regressions
Mathematical_Formulation_LaTeX: F = \frac{(RSS_C - (RSS_1 + RSS_2)) / k}{(RSS_1 + RSS_2) / (N_1 + N_2 - 2k)} \sim F(k, N_1 + N_2 - 2k)
Parameters_and_Variables: RSS_C = Residual sum of squares of pooled model; RSS_1, RSS_2 = Residual sums of squares of pre- and post-break sub-periods; k = Number of parameters; N_1, N_2 = Sample sizes.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Chow, G. C. (1960). Tests of equality between sets of coefficients in two linear regressions. Econometrica, 28(3), 591–605.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Statistically justified the Candidate B temporal demarcation point (May 1, 2022 post-mask mandate): Chow test confirms structural stability (p >= 0.15) for the post-mandate modern operational regime.

Equation_Name: CUSUM Test for Structural Parameter Stability
Parameters_and_Variables: W_t = Cumulative sum of standardized recursive residuals w_r; sigma_hat_w = Sample standard deviation of recursive residuals; k = Number of regression regressors.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Brown, R. L., Durbin, J., & Evans, J. M. (1975). Techniques for testing the constancy of regression relationships over time. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 37(2), 149–163.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Demonstrates that cumulative recursive residuals stay strictly within the 95% confidence bands from May 2022 through Dec 2025, validating model training data integrity.

Parameters_and_Variables: PAR_d = Ratio of maximum hourly throughput on day d to that day's average hourly volume; measures acute demand concentration into a single peak hour.
Published_Source_and_Citation: Standard engineering and operational metrics (Crest Factor / Peak-to-Average Ratio); Oppenheim & Schafer (2009).
Thesis_Operational_Role: Standard literature replacement for S_TSA: identifies days where checkpoint queues experience extreme surge concentration into an acute morning or evening rush hour.

Equation_Name: Volatility-Buffered Safety Capacity Lane Dimensioning Rule
Parameters_and_Variables: c(t) = Recommended integer number of open screening lanes at hour t; mu_hat_t = Expected hourly passenger arrivals; sigma_hat_t = Forecasted arrival volatility; z_q = Normal service quantile (e.g., 1.645 for 95% service level); mu_lane = Lane throughput capacity (pax/lane-hr).
Published_Source_and_Citation: Erlang, A. K. (1917); Kolesar, P., & Green, L. (1998). Insights on capacity planning using a queuing model. Management Science; Whitt, W. (1992). Understanding the efficiency of multi-server service systems. Management Science, 38(5), 708–723.
Thesis_Operational_Role: Translates volatility forecasts into actionable security checkpoint lane dimensioning in Chapter V (§5.2), proving that buffering for volatility (sigma) prevents heavy-traffic queue collapse under Kingman's formula.
